summary: Fiji's Ministry of Immigration says citizens of the countries on its visa-exempt list — among them the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, France and Germany — are not required to obtain a Fiji visa, and that visitors are given a visitor permit on immigration clearance allowing up to 4 months of stay. Nationals of countries not on the list must apply for a visa and have it approved before travel.

declarations.name: Fiji Arrival Card and Biosecurity Declaration
declarations.text: The Biosecurity Authority of Fiji says you will be given a passenger arrival card when arriving, a legal document required by law, on which you must also state any items that need to be declared. Its laws require everyone arriving from overseas to declare all biosecurity risk goods, including food, plant, plant products, used material and animal products, and undeclared risk goods must go in the amnesty bins provided. Prohibited or declarable items found that were not declared or put in the bins bring an on-the-spot fine of FJD 400, and you are also liable for prosecution with a maximum fine of FJD 20,000, a maximum of six months' imprisonment, or both.

source.name: Biosecurity Authority of Fiji — Traveling to Fiji (passenger arrival card)

currencyLimits.text: Canada's travel advice says you must make a customs declaration when in possession of currency equivalent to more than FJD 5,000 when entering Fiji and more than FJD 10,000 when exiting, and that undeclared money can lead to a fine or a prison sentence. The UK government says to declare cash in any currency worth FJD 10,000 or more.

source.name: Government of Canada — Fiji travel advice: money (customs declaration)

conflict.name: UK FCDO — Fiji travel advice (entry requirements)
conflict.states: Declare cash in any currency worth FJD 10,000 or more (no separate entry threshold).

notes: The UK government says Fiji customs has strict quarantine regulations and customs officers X-ray all luggage arriving at Nadi airport; they will confiscate most fresh foodstuffs, unless you are arriving from a country with quarantine agreements with Fiji.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are accepted by most hotels, restaurants and shops, that ATMs are widely available in main centres and some rural areas, and that some taxis only take cash payments. The UK government says not all ATMs accept the full range of bank or credit cards, and that hospitals usually ask for immediate cash payment for health services.

safety.text: The UK government says the risk of serious crime is generally low, but there are occasional incidents including sexual assault, and tells travellers to be careful of their belongings in cities and other popular tourist destinations. It warns of dangerous rip tides along reefs and river estuaries, says tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to April but cyclones occur throughout the year, and says healthcare facilities are limited in range and availability.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says the rainy and cyclone season in the Pacific Islands Region takes place from November to April, but cyclones may occur at other times. The UK government says cyclones occur throughout the year and can cause flooding and landslides that damage or block roads, and tells travellers to follow weather updates from the Fiji Meteorological Service.

The UK government says healthcare facilities in Fiji are limited in range and availability, that in serious medical emergencies people are often evacuated to another country for treatment, and that hospitals usually ask for immediate cash payment. Canada's travel advice says medical evacuation is very expensive and tells travellers to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

The UK government says to cover your shoulders and knees in rural villages and during kava ceremonies, that topless bathing and nudity in public is illegal, and that if you are invited to take part in a kava-drinking ceremony you should be aware of the potential risks of liver toxicity.

Fiji's Ministry of Immigration says the visitor permit given on immigration clearance allows up to 4 months of stay, and that the stay can be extended by 2 months if you apply for an extension and the fee is paid.

The UK government says there are dangerous rip tides along reefs and river estuaries, and that unless you have reliable local knowledge you should swim from beaches that have lifeguards on duty and follow the flag warning system.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Fiji?
faq.answer: Not if your country is on Fiji's visa-exempt list: the Ministry of Immigration says citizens of those countries — among them the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, India, France and Germany — are not required to obtain a Fiji visa, and visitors are given a visitor permit on immigration clearance allowing up to 4 months of stay. Travellers from non-visa-exempt countries must obtain an approved visa before travelling to Fiji.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Fiji?
faq.answer: Fiji's Ministry of Immigration says the visitor permit given on immigration clearance allows up to 4 months of stay, and that the stay can be extended by 2 months if you apply for an extension and the fee is paid.

faq.question: What do I need to show at Fijian immigration?
faq.answer: Fiji's Ministry of Immigration lists a passport valid for at least six months beyond the intended period of stay, funds sufficient to cover the stay, evidence of confirmed accommodation, a confirmed return or applicable onward ticket, and a visa or permit where required. The Biosecurity Authority of Fiji says you will be given a passenger arrival card when arriving, a legal document on which you must also state any items that need to be declared.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Fiji?
faq.answer: No official source we could read requires it. Canada's travel advice tells travellers to make sure they get travel insurance that includes coverage for medical evacuation and hospital stays.

faq.question: When is cyclone season in Fiji and should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the rainy and cyclone season in the Pacific Islands Region takes place from November to April, but cyclones may occur at other times. The UK government says tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to April but cyclones occur throughout the year, and that cyclones can cause flooding and landslides, often damaging or blocking roads.

Return or onward ticket: A confirmed return ticket or applicable onward travel ticket.

tips.medical-evacuation.text: Healthcare facilities are limited in range and availability. In serious medical emergencies, people are often evacuated to another country for treatment.

tips.village-etiquette.text: Topless bathing and nudity in public is illegal. Cover your shoulders and knees in rural villages and during kava ceremonies.
If you’re invited to take part in a kava-drinking ceremony, be aware of the potential risks of liver toxicity.

tips.four-month-permit.text: Others will be given visitor permits on Immigration Clearance. This visitor permit will allow a visitor up to 4 months of stay. The stay can further be extended to 2 months if applying for extension and the fee is paid.

tips.reef-and-rips.text: There are dangerous rip tides along reefs and river estuaries. Unless you have reliable local knowledge, swim from beaches that have lifeguards on duty and follow the flag warning system.

entryRequirements.passportValidity.text: Valid passport: A passport that is valid for at least six (6) months beyond the intended period of stay in Fiji.

entryRequirements.vaccinations.yellow-fe.text: To enter Fiji, you must have a certificate to prove you’ve had a yellow fever vaccination if you’re coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

entryRequirements.travelInsurance.text: Make sure you get travel insurance that includes coverage for medical evacuation and hospital stays.

entryRequirements.onwardTicket.text: Return or onward ticket: A confirmed return ticket or applicable onward travel ticket.
At Fiji border control, you must also show: an onward or return ticket a valid visa for the next country you’re travelling to

entryRequirements.proofOfFunds.text: Sufficient funds: Funds sufficient to cover the duration of stay.

entryRequirements.declarations.arrival-c.text: When arriving in Fiji you will be given a passenger arrival card. This is a legal document and it is required by law.
You must also state on this card any items that need to be declared.

Our laws require everyone arriving into Fiji from overseas to declare all biosecurity risk goods including food, plant, plant products, used material, and animal products to our Biosecurity officers at our borders.
You need to dispose off any risk goods that you have not declared on your arrival card into amnesty bins provided.

If any prohibited or declarable items are found in your baggage or possession which you have not declared on your passenger arrival card or disposed off in the Biosecurity amnesty bins provided, you will be spot fined $FJD 400. You are also liable for prosecution with a maximum fine of up to $FJD20, 000 or face a maximum of six months imprisonment or both.

entryRequirements.customs.currencyLimits.text: You must make a customs declaration when in possession of currency: equivalent to more than $5,000 FJD when entering the country equivalent to more than $10,000 FJD when exiting the country Undeclared money can lead to a fine or a prison sentence.
Declare cash in any currency worth 10,000 Fijian dollars or more.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.0.text: Fiji customs has strict quarantine regulations and customs officers X-ray all luggage arriving at Nadi airport. They will confiscate most fresh foodstuffs, unless you’re arriving from a country with quarantine agreements with Fiji.

countryFacts.payments.text: Credit cards are accepted by most hotels, restaurants, and shops. ATMs are widely available in main centres and some rural areas.
Some taxis only take cash payments.
Not all ATMs accept the full range of bank or credit cards.
Hospitals usually ask for immediate cash payment for health services.

countryFacts.safety.text: The risk of serious crime is generally low, but there are occasional incidents including sexual assault.
Be careful of your belongings in cities and other popular tourist destinations.
There are dangerous rip tides along reefs and river estuaries.
Tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to April, but cyclones occur throughout the year.
Healthcare facilities are limited in range and availability.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: The rainy and cyclone season in the Pacific Islands Region takes place from November to April, but cyclones may occur at other times.

Tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to April, but cyclones occur throughout the year. During the cyclone season there is a greater risk of strong winds and heavy rain. Cyclones can cause flooding and landslides

countryFacts.driving.text: Convention on Road Traffic Geneva, 19 September 1949
You can use a UK driving licence to drive in Fiji.
